{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has sourced evidence that buyers pay for this category. ClaireMed publishes $99/provider/month and S10.AI cites $99–$500/provider/month. Idea B shows no one paying for Pascal docs, and its own Case Against admits it.",
    "Idea A names a concrete payer with budget authority: the private practice physician or owner. Idea B's payer is speculative. The Foundation funds development, not docs, and the 'companies shipping Lazarus products' payer is never evidenced.",
    "The target is a paying customer within 90 days. Idea A's Cydoc precedent shows it is hard, but four paying customers did happen in this exact niche. Idea B has no precedent of a single paying customer.",
    "Idea A's brief proposes a concrete narrowing: a note-draft layer that pastes into existing systems, with no EHR integration, possibly limited to psych reports. That directly targets the $4–6k integration cost that sank Cydoc. Idea B's brief cites a 2012 thread suggesting the real blocker is maintainer unwillingness, which outside tooling cannot fix.",
    "Idea A's acquisition channel has sourced costs (a $1,850–$10,000 conference booth) and a precedent of actual use. Idea B's channels are unpriced organic posting and a generic, non-Pascal $2.69 CPC benchmark."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's price hypothesis of an optional ~$50/month business tier is anchored only to Read the Docs' own pricing. Nothing in the brief shows any Lazarus-based company wanting or paying for hosted docs. Its demand quotes are complaints, two of them old (2010 and a circa-2014 Reddit thread), with no indication of willingness to pay.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderately confident. Idea A wins mainly because Idea B lacks any payer, not because Idea A's evidence is strong. Idea A's demand evidence is thin: one employed PMHNP's Reddit complaint (not a buyer) and an AMA statistic relayed through competitor marketing. Its own brief documents a near-identical failure, Cydoc, with four customers and $27,900 in revenue. Idea A carries real risk from HIPAA/BAA overhead, liability concerns and long sales cycles, but it is the only one of the two with a plausible path to a paying customer in 90 days."
}
